exposure: High-dose tranexamic acid (TA) administration (4g intravenously then 1g/h for 6h)
outcome: Difference between pre- and post-delivery hemoglobin levels
cohort: The study included all women with postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) of 500 ml or more after vaginal birth.
finding: A policy of high-dose tranexamic acid in postpartum hemorrhage after vaginal deliveries was not associated with a significant reduction of blood loss, although postpartum iron sucrose injections were significantly less frequent in the TA group.
mod_finding: The study specifically investigated the efficacy of high-dose tranexamic acid in reducing blood loss only after vaginal deliveries, finding no significant reduction in this specific mode of birth.
